claims.text: Applying a PVD TiN coating to stainless steel enhances its corrosion resistance in extreme conditions.
The improved corrosion resistance results from the TiN coating creating a dense, chemically inert barrier.
Untreated stainless steel has a native passive oxide film.
The proposed TiN film is approximately 1 μm thick.
The proposed TiN film is deposited by physical vapor deposition at approximately 400°C, 3 mTorr, and 40 minutes.
High chloride concentrations, elevated temperatures, and aggressive chemicals can create conditions in which the native passive film is insufficient.
The PVD treatment produces a dense and adherent TiN coating.
The TiN coating isolates the stainless steel substrate from aggressive corrosive agents.
TiN acts as a physical corrosion barrier.
TiN is chemically inert under the proposed corrosive conditions.
The TiN coating reduces direct interactions between the stainless steel substrate and corrosive species.
Reduced interaction with corrosive species preserves the integrity of stainless steel when its passive film would otherwise degrade.
TiN-coated stainless steel will exhibit significantly greater corrosion resistance than untreated stainless steel under the same extreme conditions.
The native passive oxide film of stainless steel has reduced durability in highly aggressive chemical environments.
Mechanical stress or thermal cycling may degrade the coating and compromise its corrosion-protection effectiveness.
